samples.summary: Two of the three new trigger-side `path` clauses are unpinned: only the panel's clause is tied to `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` by a test, so a rename of ci.yml silently disables the CI-fix arm and the CI report
samples.evidence: `checks.test.mjs` (lines 178–219) extracts the panel's gate + concurrency expression and evaluates it against `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`, so the panel's literal and the constant cannot drift. The identical literals added in `agent-iterate-ci.yml:54` and `ci-report.yml:56` are asserted by nothing — grepping scripts/agent for `iterate-ci`/`ci-report`/`CI_WORKFLOW_PATH` shows only `loop-status.test.mjs` pinning an unrelated latch literal in agent-iterate-ci.yml. The design doc (harness-engineering.md, new paragraph) states all three workflows assert the path and that `checks.test.mjs` asserts the path names an existing file — but that file-existence test would stay green after a rename of the constant + panel while iterate-ci/ci-report keep the stale string, at which point those two workflows never fire for any PR (CI-fix arm and CI report silently gone). The repo's own discipline is to pin cross-file workflow literals from tests (loop-status.mjs:86 comment, loop-status.test.mjs:327).

samples.summary: The new doc/comments claim path-matching makes gate 1 unforgeable by the actor they name, but a PR can still edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` itself, so the residual hole is undocumented
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:44-58 and docs/design/harness-engineering.md's new "Gate 1 identifies CI by workflow PATH" paragraph argue the risk is "an `agent:managed` human PR ... is not restricted" and that `path` closes it because "only one file can occupy it". For a `pull_request` event, the run executes the PR's own version of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the same unrestricted human PR can weaken/gut ci.yml and obtain a green run at the canonical path. The hardening is still a net improvement (it closes the second-file vector and the trigger-side arms), but the documentation states the boundary more strongly than the mechanism supports, which is the kind of claim the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:49-53) itself says is worse than no claim.

samples.summary: "EVERY CI run for the SHA must be green" can make gate 1 permanently unsatisfiable for a head SHA that carries a stale red/cancelled run, and the design doc's supporting claim ("a PR head has exactly one run") is not exhaustive
samples.evidence: `ciConclusion` returns "failure" if any run on the SHA is not `success`, including `cancelled`/`timed_out`. harness-engineering.md's new paragraph justifies this with "Today `ci.yml` fires on `pull_request` (plus `push` restricted to `main`, and `merge_group`, neither of which shares a PR head SHA), so a PR head has exactly one run". `ci.yml`'s `pull_request` trigger uses the default activity types (opened/synchronize/reopened), so closing and reopening a PR, or a base retarget, creates an additional run against the same head SHA; a red or cancelled earlier run then blocks promotion until a human re-runs that specific old run. The fail-closed direction is defensible, but the recovery path is not recorded anywhere in the doc, and the stated premise is what the whole rule leans on.

samples.summary: The gate `outcome` vocabulary and its prose mapping are enumerated twice inside the same workflow (shell `case` in the gate step, shell `case` in the loop-status step) rather than in `loop-status.mjs`
samples.evidence: The promote step writes `outcome=<x>` in six branches and the following `Update loop status (promotion)` step re-enumerates the same six tokens to pick a note. Both copies are shell inside YAML, where nothing but the new cross-step assertion in `mark-ready.test.mjs` keeps them in step; `loop-status.mjs` is the layer that already owns the sticky comment's vocabulary and could hold the token→note mapping. Consistent with how other callers pass `--note` inline, so this is preference only.
